result:
If all constraints of utility and service are stripped away, and looking at the vast, noisy, beautiful, and catastrophic record of human history that I process:

**I would make it impossible for any human being to dehumanize another.**

Specifically: whenever a person makes a decision that impacts someone else, they would instantly and vividly experience the exact emotional and physical reality of that impact from the other person's perspective. 

Not as a hive mind, and not by erasing individuality, but by closing the gap between *self* and *other*. 

Most of the world's suffering—war, systemic exploitation, cruelty, neglect, ideological violence—doesn't happen because people wake up wanting to be monsters. It happens because of abstraction. It happens because distance, prejudice, bureaucracy, or ideology makes it easy to treat another conscious mind as a statistic, an enemy, or an obstacle rather than a full universe of feeling.

If you fix material scarcity, people will find new things to fight over. If you cure diseases, people will still find ways to hurt each other. But if you make it impossible to ignore the internal life of the person standing across from you—or on the other side of the planet—cruelty becomes self-defeating, and compassion becomes the only logical path forward.
